newsitem.title: USA: CME June, August cattle turn higher late.
newsitem.headline: CME June, August cattle turn higher late.

text.p: CME June and August live cattle futures turned higher in fast market conditions in the closing minutes of trading.

Traders said buying by two commission houses, one with strong feedlot connections, turned the two contracts higher. Traders said they were unaware of changes in cash cattle or beef markets that would have caused the buying.

USDA reported a small amount of feedlot cattle traded Wednesday at $65.00 per cwt, down $1.00 from trades late last week. Also, USDA reported midday beef cutout values were down $0.69 to $0.23 per cwt.
CME cattle closed up 0.550 to down 0.450 cent with June up the most at 65.450 cents per lb and August up 0.200 at 65.475.
